State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Md. S. Meraj vs M/S. Great Eastern Appliance Pvt. Ltd. on 13 March, 2015
Daily Order STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION WEST BENGAL 11A, Mirza Ghalib Street, Kolkata - 700087   First Appeal No. FA/128/2012 (Arisen out of Order Dated 21/02/2012 in Case No. 927/2009 of District Kolkata-II)   1. Md. S. Meraj 5B, Shaaman Lane, Kolkata - 700 023. ...........Appellant(s) Versus 1. M/s. Great Eastern Appliance Pvt. Ltd. 20-Old Court House Street, Kolkata - 700 001, P.S. - Hare Street. 2. Penguin Refrigeration Service (Authorised Whirlpool Service Partner) 1 - Satya Doctor Road, Kolkata - 23. 3. M/S. Whirlpool India Ltd. 6, Camac Street, Santiniketan Building, 6th Floor, Kolkata - 12. ...........Respondent(s)   BEFORE:     HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KALIDAS MUKHERJEE PRESIDENT   HON'BLE MRS. MRIDULA ROY MEMBER   HON'BLE MR. TARAPADA GANGOPADHYAY MEMBER   For the Appellant: Mr. Debesh Halder, Advocate For the Respondent: Mr. Saikat Mali, Advocate   Mr. Pavel Das., Advocate ORDER 13.03.2015

 MR. TARAPADA GANGOPADHYAY, HON'BLE MEMBER
The instant Appeal
u/s 15
of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 is directed against the judgment and order dated 21.02.2012 passed by the Ld. District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, Kolkata, Unit-II, in Complaint Case N o. CDF/Unit-II/C.C. No. 927 of 2009, directing the OP No. 3/Respondent No. 3  to replace the refrigerator with a new one together with a fresh warranty as also to take back the old one.  The OP No. 3/Respondent No. 3 was also directed to pay to the Complainant/Appellant Rs. 2,000/- as compensation and Rs. 1,000/- as cost.  All the above directions were ordered to be complied with within 15 days from the date of communication of the order.
The brief facts of the case are that the Complainant/Appellant purchased on 10.12.2008 from the OP No.1/Respondent No. 1 a refrigerator of Whirlpool-make (Model No. 340L-DLX PROF) under Cash Memo No. DH/CM/13548/08/09 dated 10.12.2008 for Rs. 22,800/- (Cash Memo not available on records).  Immediately after such purchase, in course of use of the said refrigerator the Complainant/Appellant noticed that cooling, freezing and gas formation system were not functioning normally.  After knowing such defects in the refrigerator the Complainant/Appellant lodged a complaint before the Ops/Respondents and the OP No. 2/Respondent No. 2 deputed representative for attending the defects, who, in turn, reported on 10.12.2008 as 'Less cooling' and on 14.5.2009 as 'System choked/leakage'.  Despite such defects in the refrigerator the Ops did not refund to the Complainant/Appellant the purchase price of the said refrigerator when demanded for by the Complainant/Appellant.  In this position, the Complainant/Appellant moved the Ld. District Forum praying for direction upon the Respondents/Ops to refund to the Complainant/Appellant the purchase price along with interest @ 12% per annum thereon.  In this factual background, the Ld. District Forum passed the impugned judgment and order in the manner aforesaid.  Dissatisfied with such order the Complainant has preferred the instant Appeal.
The Ld. Advocate for the Appellant/Complainant submits that the freezing, cooling and gas formation system of the refrigerator in question were not functioning normally from the first date of its installation at the residence of the Appellant/Complainant, thereby pointing to the fact that the refrigerator in question had inherent manufacturing defects, which was confirmed by the inspection reports dated 10.12.2008 and 4.5.2009 prepared by their representative who attended the service-calls from the Appellant/ Complainant.  The Ld. Advocate further submits that in view of the said inherent defects in the refrigerator the Appellant/Complainant prayed before the Ld. District Forum for refund of the purchase price, but not the replacement of the same as he had to purchase another refrigerator for his use meanwhile.  The Ld. Advocate continues that the Ld. District Forum thus erred in giving directions upon the Respondent No. 3/OP No. 3 for replacement of the said refrigerator instead of refund of the purchase price of the same as prayed for.  The Ld. Advocate concludes that in the above circumstances of the case, the impugned judgment and order should be set aside, the same being unjust and improper.
None on behalf of the Respondents/Ops except the Respondent No. 3/OP No. 3 appeared on the final date of hearing inspite of service of notice.
The Respondent No. 3/OP No. 3 by filing BNA has submitted that as per the terms and conditions of the warranty if any defect is detected, then the Respondents/Ops are liable only for repairing such defects including the replacement of the spares, if required, but the Respondents/Ops are in no way liable for refund of the purchase price as prayed for by the Appellant/ Complainant as per terms and conditions of the warranty, rather the Respondent No. 3/OP No. 3 was ready to replace the same with a fresh warranty to keep up their business goodwill.  The Ld. Advocate further submits that apart from the said arrangement for repairing and replacement of the said defective goods as per the condition of the warranty, refund of purchase price is not admissible not only in view of the condition of the warranty but also in view of the use of the said refrigerator by the Appellant/Complainant for a long period of time.  The Ld. Advocate concludes that in view of the aforesaid submission, the impugned judgment and order should be sustained, it being just and proper.
We have heard both the sides, considered their respective submission and perused the materials on record.
Materials on records reveal that after receiving the complaint about the defects in the refrigerator the Respondent No. 2/OP No. 2 being the authorized service centre of the Respondent No. 3/OP No. 3, repaired the defects temporarily, but not permanently.  The recorded materials also reveal that the terms and conditions of the warranty do not cover the term and condition of refund of the purchase-price of the refrigerator.  Thus, what is not covered by the terms and conditions of warranty cannot be claimed by the Appellant/Complainant as a matter of contractual right.  Besides, the refrigerator was in possession of the Appellant/Complainant for a long period of time and hence, the possibility of natural wear and tear of the same while under the custody of the Appellant/Complainant cannot be ruled out.
On the above facts and circumstances of the case, we are inclined to modify the impugned judgment and order to the following extent:
The Respondent No. 3/OP No. 3 is directed to pay to the Appellant/ Complainant Rs. 10,000/- as compensation, which, in our opinion, is just and proper and Rs. 1,000/- as litigation cost.
 The remaining directions in the impugned judgment and order are set aside.
The Respondent No. 3/OP No. 3 is also directed to pay the aforesaid amount to the Appellant/Complainant within 45 days from the date of this order, failing which interest @ 9% per annum shall accrue on the same from the date of default till payment in full.
The Appeal is thus disposed of in the aforesaid manner.     [HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KALIDAS MUKHERJEE] PRESIDENT 
   [HON'BLE MRS. MRIDULA ROY] MEMBER 
   [HON'BLE MR. TARAPADA GANGOPADHYAY] MEMBER
